market.advice: The tape closed higher and almost none of that matters next to what happened underneath it. SPY finished at 769.10, up about 0.2%, 1.1% off its high and comfortably above a rising 50-day at 750.17, with the distribution-day count still at zero and VIX easing to 15.1 against a 15.0 five-day average. QQQ closed at 716.08, slightly lower on the day - the index snapped a three-day losing streak on the back of everything except technology. Breadth improved a single point to 57% of the 450 scanned names above their 50-day, and the signal split is 157 STRONG BUY, 124 WATCH, 137 WEAK. By every structural measure this is a healthy uptrend. Two things drove the session and both rewrote the leaderboard. First, bonds rallied, which is the exact inverse of yesterday's setup where climbing yields broke technology. Lower yields bid every rate-sensitive corner of the market: Real Estate averaged +1.2% (ARE +10.3%, CSGP +7.5%), homebuilders ripped (DHI +4.2%, PHM +3.7%, LOW +2.4%), and 27 names upgraded from WATCH or WEAK to STRONG BUY - overwhelmingly staples, REITs and builders. The same move went through banks in reverse, because lower yields compress net interest margin: Financial Services averaged -1.2% with FITB -4.1%, AFL -4.3%, CFG -3.7%, C -3.5%, USB -3.0% and PNC -3.0%. Second, Moderna reported positive results for its cancer vaccine developed with Merck, and MRNA closed +177% at 174.38 on 12.8x average volume. MRK rose 12.6% to a new high at 152.23. The whole complex followed - Healthcare averaged +5.4% across 51 names, the largest sector move on the board, with ILMN +8.9%, DHR +6.1%, A +4.7%, VRTX +4.5%, LLY +4.5%, BIIB +4.2% and AMGN +4.0%. What paid for all of it was AI hardware. Technology's -0.2% average hides a genuine unwind in memory, storage and semicap: STX -7.9%, WDC -6.9%, LRCX -6.3%, KEYS -6.3%, NTAP -5.0%, AVGO -4.6%, INTC -4.0%, KLAC -3.9%, AMD -3.7%, AMAT -3.5%. Cybersecurity went with it (CRWD -5.3%, PANW -3.8%) and so did the industrial complex leaders (GE -5.0%, NUE -5.9%, CAT -3.0%). MRVL +9.9% was the lone semiconductor winner and it was a share-shift story, not a sector bid - Marvell taking Google silicon business from Broadcom, which is precisely why AVGO fell. Energy simply paused, averaging -0.1% after its run, though it still converts 75% of its 20 names to STRONG BUY, the best in the market; crude settled near a four-week high, Hormuz traffic remains slowed and the UAE has now placed a financial embargo on Iran, so the supply risk is unresolved rather than resolved. Sector conversion into the next session reads Energy 75%, Basic Materials 50%, Financials 46%, Healthcare 44%, Consumer Defensive 44%, Industrials 39%, Consumer Cyclical 34%, Technology 29%, Real Estate 21%, Utilities 9% and Communication Services 0 of 10. How to trade it: keep normal position sizing, because nothing in the index structure argues for defence. Do not chase healthcare - the sector that moved 5.4% in a day is the worst place to put new money tomorrow, and the two names that led it (MRNA at RSI 93.9, MRK at RSI 87.5) are the two you should least want to buy. The better use of the session is that it handed you pullbacks: the highest-scoring banks and industrials sold off into their 50-day moving averages while their fundamentals did not change, and that is where the risk-defined entries are. Leave memory, storage and semicap alone until the group stops making lower lows. Finally, respect the calendar - there is a heavy earnings cluster inside the next fifteen sessions (SJM 7 days, CRWD, NVDA, CRM and A at 8, MRVL, WDAY and RBRK at 9, SAIC 12, DELL and PANW 14, NTAP, SNOW, HPE and CPB at 15). Several of the highest scores in this scan sit directly on top of a print, which is why they are marked WATCH rather than STRONG BUY.
